title: Near-linear-space exact planar distance oracles with polylogarithmic queries
formal: Does every directed planar graph with n vertices and nonnegative real edge weights admit a uniformly constructible exact distance oracle using \(O(n\log^c(2+n))\) cells, answering each distance query in \(O(\log^c(2+n))\) worst-case operations, and having expected polynomial preprocessing time, for one absolute constant c? Preprocessing may be Las Vegas randomized, but every returned oracle must answer all pairs exactly.
definitions:
The input is a finite directed graph whose underlying undirected graph is simple and planar, together with a combinatorial planar embedding and its nonnegative finite real edge weights. Either or both directions of an underlying edge may be present. There are O(n) arcs. A query supplies an ordered pair u,v and asks for the minimum sum of weights along a directed path, infinity if v is unreachable from u, and zero for u=v. No path output is required.

The arithmetic RAM has one cell per real weight and \(\Theta(\log n)\)-bit words for labels and polynomial-size memory addresses. Exact arithmetic, comparisons, word operations and memory access cost one; arbitrary encoding of a whole graph into a real with unit-cost decoding is disallowed. All persistent graph data and auxiliary tables count toward storage. The query cannot access an uncharged original graph.

A single finite preprocessing algorithm must work for every input, terminate almost surely, and have expected cost \(n^{O(1)}\) over its internal coins on each graph. Every oracle returned must obey the space and exact-query guarantees; query time is deterministic worst-case after preprocessing. This explicitly permits random construction without allowing erroneous distance answers.

Both logarithmic overheads must have fixed exponents. A space bound \(n^{1+o(1)}\) is not necessarily \(n\operatorname{polylog}n\), and a query time \(n^{o(1)}\) is not necessarily polylogarithmic. Exactness is about arbitrary real distances in the arithmetic model, not decimal output precision. The planarity promise alone supplies no bounded-diameter, bounded-treewidth or undirected-distance assumption.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked construction with the simultaneous near-linear-space, polylogarithmic-query and polynomial-preprocessing guarantees, or its negation in the stated model. Exact oracles with a subpolynomial overhead in one resource do not automatically qualify. Approximate planar distances or an uncharged quadratic distance table do not establish the proposition.
context:
The 2023 JACM synthesis gives almost-optimal exact planar distance oracles: one resource can have only logarithmic overhead while the other retains a subpolynomial factor. Its conclusion explicitly asks for near-linear space and polylogarithmic queries simultaneously.

The March 2026 preprint improves construction time for the almost-optimal space/query tradeoff. Its abstract retains n^(1+o(1)) space, so the stronger polylogarithmic-overhead storage target is not resolved merely by that headline.
why: This asks whether planarity permits simultaneously compact and fast exact distance queries.

import_provenance.original_title: Near-linear-space exact planar distance oracles with polylogarithmic queries
import_provenance.original_statement: Can every weighted directed planar graph admit an exact distance oracle using O(n polylog n) space and polylogarithmic query time, with polynomial preprocessing? Wulff-Nilsen’s exact-oracle work and subsequent tradeoffs leave this combination of space and query bounds unresolved.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: Linear space and constant query time are known for fixed-error approximate undirected planar distances. The exact-distance requirement is essential; assume nonnegative edge weights.

sentences: A directed planar graph is compressed into a structure answering exact distance queries.
The target permits only logarithmic overhead over linear space and logarithmic query cost.
It includes unreachable pairs and arbitrary nonnegative weights in an exact arithmetic model.
Known almost-optimal tradeoffs and the 2026 construction improvement retain a subpolynomial factor.
The question asks whether planarity permits exact distances with both resources simultaneously near their natural minimum.
